chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one who approaches the animal and penetrates, he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the Penalty (Hadd).

key_terms.الْبَهِيمَةَ: The animal (specifically in the context of sexual intercourse)
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The Hadd (fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia)
key_terms.فَيُولِجُ: And he penetrates (referring to the act of intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal penalty for bestiality according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the general principle that the fixed penalty (Hadd) applies to bestiality, a ruling that later jurists debated regarding whether it mirrors the penalty for human adultery or constitutes a distinct category. It is transmitted through the reliable chain of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, a key figure in Shia hadith transmission, underscoring the early juristic consensus on this matter. The ruling highlights the sanctity of the animal as a subject of legal accountability in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the one who goes to the animals, so he penetrates. Heasws said: ‘Upon him is the Penalty (Hadd)’.
